title: Day and Trial Passes: basis for recording a refund
content:
This document states the basis on which a refund is recorded for a Day and Trial Passes pass (Single Day Pass, Three-Day Trial Pass, Seven-Day Trial Pass, Weekly Visitor Pass, Monthly Trial Pass, Corporate Guest Pass).

## Rule
A refund may be recorded only while the pass is active, or in the same moment as its confirmed cancellation to closed. It may be recorded only when the tier's basis allows a refund after a visit has been used, or no visit on the pass has yet been used. It may be recorded only when the request is made no later than the tier's refund window of elapsed hours after the pass was purchased, that elapsed time counted in whole hours from the purchase date with no rounding down; a request made exactly at that many hours still qualifies, since the boundary is inclusive.

## Eligibility checklist
- Pass status: the company's own current record of the pass's status, correlated to the same pass the refund is requested against, must show the pass as active, or as closed in the same moment as a confirmed cancellation. A status of applied, expired, or closed other than through that same confirmed cancellation does not satisfy this condition.
- Usage: either the tier's basis allows a refund after a visit has been used, or the system's record shows no visit yet used on the pass.
- Timing: the request must be made no later than the tier's refund window, counted in elapsed hours from the date the pass was purchased (with no rounding down of partial hours), after that purchase date; a request made exactly at that boundary still qualifies, and any request later than the boundary does not.

### Boundary illustration (hypothetical)
For any tier, take the purchase date as the anchor and the tier's own refund window in hours as the allowed span. A refund requested at the instant the elapsed time since purchase exactly equals that window is still within the window and qualifies (the boundary is inclusive). A refund requested even one minute past that same instant no longer qualifies, because the elapsed time then exceeds the window.
